title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction + spillover scheduling to reduce fragmentation and OOMs
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: production workloads have been hitting KV cache fragmentation and memory-pressure OOMs during long-context sessions and adversarial prefix churn. This PR implements an adaptive eviction + spillover scheduling system aimed at reducing fragmentation and improving tail latency under continuous batching.

What this changes (summary): 1) Adaptive eviction policy that combines size-weighted recency + token-length weighting to avoid evicting long KV entries that are cheap to keep around; 2) A spillover pager that asynchronously moves cold KV shards to host memory (CPU) and fetches them on demand, rather than immediate eviction; 3) Background defragmentation/compaction scheduler that cooperates with the runtime's continuous-batching hot path so compaction work is deferred to safe windows; 4) A compacting allocator (segregated free lists) to reduce internal fragmentation for variable-sized KV entries; 5) New metrics and tracing hooks for spill/restore events and compaction latency; 6) Unit and microbench tests + perf harness updates.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4271) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Microbenchmark for evict/restore latency - [x] Perf runs in perf-canary (baseline vs v2) - [x] Docs update (KV cache observability)

Behavioral notes: The default for Dedicated/Hosted clusters will enable spillover but keep aggressive avoidance of synchronous restores for latency-sensitive routes. Customers can opt into eager-restore mode via config. The pager has throttles to prevent hot-path restoration storms and will fall back to eviction when synchronous memory cannot be satisfied.

Compatibility: config knobs are additive; no breaking API changes. The allocator changes are internal to the runtime binary and guarded behind a feature flag (kv.compaction.enabled) that is on for canary clusters and off for older releases until validated.

Benchmarks: perf-canary runs with a mix of 1k simultaneous chat sessions, sequence length ~6k tokens: - Cache-induced stall events: down 72% - OOM incidents on stress runs: down 90% - 99th percentile token latency (in heavy-churn scenarios): improved by ~18%

Why this approach: previous LRU-only strategies led to churn of large KV entries and exacerbated fragmentation. Moving cold shards to host memory avoids unnecessary re-computation and gives better tail behavior without increasing steady-state GPU memory usage. Coordinating compaction with scheduler windows avoids interfering with continuous batching (the hot path).

release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: adaptive eviction reduces fragmentation and OOMs; asynchronous spillover moves cold KV shards to host memory to improve tail latency; background compaction reduces internal fragmentation. Config flags: kv.compaction.enabled (default: on for canary), kv.spill.mode (default: async).
testing_notes: Added unit tests for eviction heuristics and restore coalescing; microbench harness and perf-canary config included. See perf/microbench/README for repro steps.
maintainer_notes: Feature gated behind kv.compaction.enabled. Rollout plan: enable on canary -> monitor kv.restore.latency and kv.compact.duration -> gradual rollout to Dedicated clusters. If restore storms are observed, toggle kv.spill.mode to eager-evict and open support ticket SUP-1123.
